title: My friend fixes boards for fun, so I made a repair game
author: Bill_Buffet
selftext:
A friend of mine repairs circuit boards as a hobby. Watching him bring a dead board back to life with just a multimeter and a soldering iron looked like magic to me, and I wanted to understand how he does it.

So I built DEADBOARD, a free educational game where you get a broken board on a virtual bench. You measure, find the fault, fix it, and prove the repair works. It starts with simple circuits and goes all the way up to a real open-source laptop mainboard (the video shows that one).

Each board works like a CTF challenge: fix every fault and a hidden flag unlocks. You can also plant faults in your own boards and share them as challenges for others to crack.

It runs in the browser, nothing to install:

[https://tholtman1-del.github.io/deadboard/](https://tholtman1-del.github.io/deadboard/)

It's open source too: [https://github.com/tholtman1-del/deadboard](https://github.com/tholtman1-del/deadboard)

If you repair boards yourself, I'd love to hear what feels wrong or missing.
